drivingQuestion: When more than one bidder reneges, is the treasury's loss borne by the highest reneging bidder alone or divided among them?
outcomeNote: Rav Ḥisda's distinction between simultaneous and successive reneging is adopted, confirmed by a baraita, and repeated in the variant version.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The mishna teaches that if one said: The field is mine for ten sela, and another said for twenty, and another said thirty, and another said forty, and yet another said fifty; and then the one who bid fifty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela, and it is redeemed by the one who bid forty. In this manner, the Temple treasury does not lose. «Rav Ḥisda says:» The mishna «taught» that the treasurer repossesses ten sela from the one who initially offered fifty sela «only when the one who» offered «forty stands in his place» and intends to purchase the field, as the Temple treasury would have lost only ten sela.

segments.he: אֲבָל אֵין בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶן.
segments.en: «But» if «the one who» offered «forty does not stand in his place,» i.e., he too reneged on his offer, then the additional amount they had offered is «divided between» the one who initially offered fifty and the one who offered forty, as follows: The one who offered fifty pays all ten of the difference between fifty and forty, but he must also pay half of the extra ten that is the difference between the offer of forty and the previous offer of thirty. The reason is that the one who bid fifty agreed to that extra ten that raised the price from thirty to forty. In sum, the one who offered fifty pays fifteen, and the one who said forty pays five.

segments.he: תְּנַן: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל אַרְבָּעִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין עַד עֶשֶׂר. אַמַּאי? לִיתֵּן בַּר חַמְשִׁין בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים.
segments.en: The Gemara raises an objection to the statement of Rav Ḥisda from that which «we learned» in the mishna: If the one who bid «forty reneged» on his offer, the treasurer «repossesses from his property up to ten» sela. The Gemara explains the objection: According to Rav Ḥisda, there is a difficulty: «Why» does the mishna rule that his property is repossessed by ten sela? «Let the one who» offered «fifty give together with him,» and therefore the one who offered forty should give only five. The Gemara responds: The mishna is referring to a case «where there is no one who» offered «fifty» sela.

segments.he: חָזַר בּוֹ בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, אַמַּאי? וְלִיתֵּן דְּבֶן אַרְבָּעִים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים. חָזַר בּוֹ בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, אַמַּאי? לִיתֵּן דְּבֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים.
segments.en: The Gemara further objects: The mishna also teaches that if the one who bid «thirty reneged» on his offer, the treasurer «repossesses from his property up to ten» sela. But according to Rav Ḥisda, «why» is only his property repossessed? «Let» the one «who» offered «forty give together with him.» The Gemara again responds: The mishna is referring to a case «where there is no one who» offered «forty» sela. The Gemara persists: The mishna states that if the one who bid «twenty reneged» on his offer, the treasurer «repossesses from his property up to ten» sela. According to Rav Ḥisda, «why» is only his property repossessed? «Let» the one «who» offered «thirty give together with him.» Once again, the Gemara responds: The mishna is referring to a case «where there is no one who» offered «thirty» sela.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר, מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשׇׁוְיָהּ וְנִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֶשֶׂר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר, לִיתֵּב דְּבֶן עֶשְׂרִים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים, אִי הָכִי, ״נִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֲשָׂרָה״ — ״נִפְרָעִין מִמֶּנּוּ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If so,» then «say the latter clause» of the mishna: If the one who bid «ten reneged» on his offer, the treasurer «sells» the field «at its value and collects the remainder from» the property «of the one» who bid «ten,» to complete the sum of ten sela. Why is payment collected only from the one who offered ten? «Let the one who» offered «twenty give together with him. And if you would say that here too, there is no one who» offered «twenty» sela, then «if so,» why does the mishna state: And «collects from» the one who bid «ten?» The mishna «should have» stated simply: And «collects from him,» as there is no one else who submitted an offer.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּבַת אַחַת, כָּאן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: חָזְרוּ כּוּלָּן כְּאֶחָד — מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶם. וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן: מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Ḥisda said:» This is «not difficult. Here,» when the potential loss incurred by the Temple treasury is divided, they reneged on their offers «simultaneously;» whereas «there,» in the mishna, where only one individual must cover the loss, two individuals reneged «one after the other.» The Gemara notes that «this is also taught» in a baraita: If «all of them reneged at once they divide» the potential loss incurred by the Temple treasury «between them.» Now «didn’t we learn» in the mishna: The treasurer «repossesses from his property up to ten» sela, without any mention of a division? «Rather,» must one «not conclude from» the baraita that the halakha is «in accordance with» the statement of «Rav Ḥisda,» who holds that when two individuals renege on their offers simultaneously they divide the loss between them? The Gemara comments: Indeed, «conclude from it» that this is the case.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּרָמֵי לְהוּ מִירְמָא: תְּנַן: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר, מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשׇׁוְיָהּ וְנִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֶשֶׂר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר, וְהָתַנְיָא: מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶם! אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — בְּבַת אַחַת, כָּאן — בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה.
segments.en: The Gemara notes that «there are» those «who raise» this baraita as a contradiction: «We learned» in the mishna that if the one «who» bid «ten reneged» on his offer, the treasurer «sells» the field «at its value and collects the remainder from» the property «of the one» who bid «ten. But isn’t it taught» in a baraita that «they divide» the potential loss to the Temple treasury «between them? Rav Ḥisda said:» This is «not difficult. Here» in the baraita they reneged on their offers «simultaneously,» whereas «there,» in the mishna, two individuals reneged «one after the other.»

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: לא שנו אלא שבן ארבעים עומד במקומו
moves.summary: narrows the mishna's distraint rule to where the next bidder holds firm
moves.about: the mishna's rule that only the reneging bidder is distrained ten sela applies only where the next-lower bidder stands by his offer

moves.cueHe: אבל אין בן ארבעים עומד במקומו
moves.summary: otherwise the two reneging bidders divide the loss
objects from the mishna's forty-bidder clause
moves.about: on Rav Ḥisda's view the fifty-bidder should share the loss, yet the mishna distrains the forty-bidder for the whole ten

moves.summary: there is no fifty-bidder in that case
moves.about: the mishna's clause speaks of a case where no fifty-bidder is present

moves.cueHe: חזר בו בן שלשים — ממשכנין מנכסיו עד עשר, אמאי?
moves.summary: presses the same from the thirty- and twenty-bidder clauses
moves.about: the same difficulty from the mishna's clauses about the thirty-bidder and the twenty-bidder reneging

moves.summary: each clause likewise lacks the next-higher bidder
moves.about: each such clause likewise speaks where the next-higher bidder is absent

moves.summary: the repeated answer fails on the mishna's last clause
moves.about: if every clause speaks where no higher bidder exists, the last clause's 'we collect from the one who bid ten' should have read 'we collect from him'

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא הכא נמי דליכא בן עשרים
moves.summary: floats that here too no twenty-bidder is present
moves.about: a defence the sugya entertains and then discards — that here too no twenty-bidder is present

moves.summary: the mishna's own wording rules that float out
moves.about: the mishna's wording 'we collect from the one who bid ten' rules out a case with no other bidder, since it should then have said 'from him'

moves.cueHe: אלא אמר רב חסדא: לא קשיא, כאן בבת אחת, כאן בזה אחר זה
moves.summary: Rav Ḥisda re-grounds his ruling on simultaneous versus successive reneging
moves.about: the loss is shared where the bidders reneged simultaneously, and borne alone where they reneged one after another

moves.summary: a baraita teaches that all who reneged at once divide the loss
moves.about: brings a baraita teaching that if all reneged at once they divide the loss

moves.cueHe: והא אנן תנן: ממשכנין מנכסיו עד עשר!
moves.summary: but the mishna knows no division of the loss
moves.about: the baraita has the loss divided while the mishna distrains one bidder alone

moves.cueHe: אלא לאו שמע מינה כדרב חסדא, שמע מינה
moves.summary: only Rav Ḥisda's distinction reconciles them, so it stands
moves.about: the baraita's ruling for simultaneous reneging supports Rav Ḥisda's distinction

moves.summary: a second version sets mishna against baraita directly
moves.about: a second version of the discussion, setting the mishna's collection from the ten-bidder alone directly against the baraita's division of the loss

moves.cueHe: אמר רב חסדא: לא קשיא, כאן — בבת אחת
moves.summary: the same distinction resolves the contradiction in that version too
moves.about: the baraita speaks of simultaneous reneging and the mishna of successive reneging
